value.title: Cross-model review R3 — 132-spawn-reports-bind @ 46a2d862
value.note: VERDICT: APPROVE — no blocking findings remain. Delta review of ac7cfe46..46a2d862 as scoped by the PM (worker change plus fresh gates), with re-adjudication of the carried set. The R2 blocker N1 is verified FIXED from source, and its witness discriminates all three plausible wrong answers rather than one. FRESH GATE RECEIPTS taken by this reviewer at 46a2d862: `cargo test --workspace` EXIT 0, 610 passed, 0 failed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` EXIT 0; `cargo test -p pij-daemon pointer::worker::tests` 27 passed, 0 failed — independently confirming the PM's corrected count of 27 rather than the initially reported 28. AC VERDICTS UNCHANGED FROM R2: AC1a, AC1b, AC2, AC3, AC4 TRUE; AC5 TRUE with the split-evidence caveat at N4, which the N1 fix turns into a three-case table (proven-absent terminalizes, tombstoned terminalizes even under unknown inventory, unproven absence retries). REMAINING OPEN ITEMS ARE ALL NON-BLOCKING and were graded so in R2: R003, R004, R005, R007, R008, plus the questions N2, N3, N4, N5, N6 and the friction note R010. This round also records a CORRECTION OF MY OWN R2 WORDING at N8. Two items are addressed to prime rather than the PM: R003 is a G1 promise that no acceptance criterion asserts, so the AC set cannot catch it; and N2 and N6 are questions about the intent of a ruling, not defects in its implementation.

value.finding: FIXED, and fixed in the right shape. list_panes now yields Option<Vec<Pane>> where None means UNKNOWN INVENTORY rather than an empty roster, which is the same absent-versus-observed-absence distinction that made the R001 fix correct. Three properties I asked for are all present: (1) the systemic error is DEFERRED, NOT SWALLOWED — `deferred` is pre-seeded with the inventory error and drain_once still returns it after the pass, so a tmux outage stays visible to the resilient outer loop; (2) the pane-absence terminal policy is SKIPPED for that pass — `live_panes.is_some_and(...)` is false under None, so a pane-absent recipient falls through to release_or_backoff and RETRIES rather than being terminalized on unproven absence; (3) tombstoned recipients still terminalize under unknown inventory, which is correct because a tombstone is a registry fact that needs no tmux. `deferred.get_or_insert` keeps the FIRST error, so the systemic cause wins over any per-recipient consequence — the right choice. I checked for any remaining tmux call that can still abort the pass: none. handle_claim's fresh_injection_verdict errors still route through backoff into `deferred` and the pass continues.

value.finding: The N1 witness is a real witness, and it discriminates both failure modes rather than one. pane_inventory_failure_is_deferred_while_recipient_work_continues asserts DELIVERY CONTENT (both recipients' messages present in transport.delivered()), not the handled count — which was the specific thing I asked for, because a pass that claimed both and delivered to neither would satisfy a count. It also asserts expect_err with the scripted message, so the opposite failure — silently swallowing the systemic error — fails the test too. And it discriminates the subtle wrong fix: because both panes ARE registered and listed, treating a failed inventory as an EMPTY roster would terminalize both and drive delivered.len() to 0. RED grading, stated precisely: the recorded RED (left 0, right 2) is ENTAILED by the pre-fix control flow I read at ac7cfe46 — `let live_panes = self.tmux.list_panes().await?;` returns before any claim, so delivered is necessarily empty. I did not re-execute it, and note that reproducing it required back-porting the new FakeTmux::with_list_pane_failures, which did not exist on the pre-fix tree.

value.finding: CORRECTION TO MY OWN R2 FINDING, plus a small residual. In R2 I wrote that a_recipient_whose_pane_has_vanished_does_not_starve_the_queue_behind_it is 'present and no longer load-bearing'. That was too strong and I withdraw it. Re-examined at HEAD: its dead recipient still reaches fail_claim and the live recipient behind it still delivers in the same pass, so its ASSERTION genuinely exercises pass-continuation-past-a-dead-recipient and remains load-bearing for that property. What is actually stale is its DOC COMMENT, which narrates a mechanism the test no longer traverses — it describes permits_injection_fresh answering 'can't find pane: %1861' and the `?` on handle_claim ending the pass, and neither happens now, because the pane check short-circuits to fail_claim first. So the third item in my R2 note (re-point that test so it can go red again) is largely satisfied by the new N1 witness covering the tmux-error path; what remains is comment drift, which matters only because that comment is the institutional memory of a 29-hour production starvation. Smallest fix: a two-line amendment saying the tmux-error half of this story now lives in pane_inventory_failure_is_deferred_while_recipient_work_continues.

value.finding: CONFIRMED OPEN, unchanged in R3 and graded non-blocking in R2, so not re-escalated here. spawn_failure still returns Envelope::refused with data:None, leaving dispatched/bound/pane/pid as prose in meta on every failure path. Recorded for prime rather than the PM: G1 promises those structured fields on the failure path and the code does not deliver them, yet NO ACCEPTANCE CRITERION asserts it — AC1a and AC1b both check the failure's CONTENT (mismatch text, exit code, log tail) and never its SHAPE. So this gap cannot be caught by satisfying the AC set, which is a plan-coverage issue as much as a code one.

value.finding: CONFIRMED OPEN, and now BOUNDED by the N1 fix in one useful respect: terminalization on pane absence requires a SUCCESSFUL inventory, so a tmux blip no longer contributes false terminal failures. The residual stands unchanged — the check runs before the proc check and so applies to bound seats, and fail_claim is terminal, so a pane that dies during a revive window still converts recoverable queued messages into permanent failures. Ruled scope, so this is an acknowledgement item rather than a defect to fix in this plan.

value.finding: CONFIRMED OPEN, unchanged. Spawn evidence files under temp_dir()/pij-rs-spawn/ leak on the no_wait path and on every revive.

QUESTION FOR JORDAN, carried forward unchanged and still not a defect. Pane-absence terminalization precedes transport capability, while the real UdsTransport resolves by PID first and does not need the pane, so a genuinely socket-reachable Claude seat loses a deliverable message when its pane is gone. The author's own test deliberately covers a socket-capable bound recipient, so this is the ruled policy; only the intent needs confirming. If it was not intended, the fix is one can_deliver probe before terminalizing.

CARRIED FORWARD, and now the more worthwhile of the two documentation items. AC5 claims both halves of G6, but the production-copy baseline reports tombstoned:0, so the pane-absent half is production-proven while the tombstone half rests on one unit test. The N1 fix adds a third state to this story — under unknown inventory tombstones still terminalize and pane-absence does not — so the evidence table now has three cases and should say which of them production actually exercised.
